title: 1,000 Agent Tasks in a Sandbox: What Breaks When LLMs Run Code — Kevin Orellana, AWS
talk_summary: An AWS engineer pointed a coding agent at their sandbox platform through an MCP server, generated 1,000 tests across 10 domains, stored results in SQLite, and ran concurrent subagents to find failures. The failures clustered at the MCP/interface layer and at sandbox primitives such as encoding, filesystem persistence, memory, permissions, and tool parity, so the practical lesson is to fuzz-test remote sandboxes with realistic workflows and classify failures by layer.

takeaways.what_they_do: They exposed the sandbox through an MCP server, had a coding agent generate and run 1,000 tests across 10 domains, stored results in SQLite, and used concurrent subagents to execute tests.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we asked to just plainly write a thousand tests across 10 domains
takeaways.numbers: 1,000 tests across 10 domains; took a few hours and was token-heavy

takeaways.technique: Classify failures by interface vs sandbox layer
takeaways.what_they_do: They separated failures into MCP/interface-layer bugs and sandbox-layer bugs, which made it clearer whether the agent was blocked by tool encoding or by VM/filesystem/resource constraints.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we started to segregate the patterns uh and failures into two layers. One was at the interface and the other one was at the sandbox layer
takeaways.numbers: three highlighted failures: image encoding mismatch, null byte issue, files written to a directory not retrievable

takeaways.what_they_do: They uploaded and downloaded an image to check round-trip fidelity and found the MCP encoding layer was incorrect; a null byte also broke tests.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we found that the encoding layer at the MCP layer was incorrect
takeaways.numbers: image upload/download mismatch; null byte caused test failures

takeaways.what_they_do: They compared a code sandbox and a cloud browser and found browser tests failed heavily due to memory constraints while the code interpreter did not show the same fault.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a lot of our tests fail just due to memory constraints
takeaways.numbers: cloud browser tests failed due to memory constraints; code interpreter did not show that fault

takeaways.technique: Structured result store for concurrent subagents
takeaways.what_they_do: They used SQLite instead of markdown because agents tend to write markdown files, which does not scale for 1,000 tests; SQLite let multiple subagents store results concurrently.
takeaways.evidence_quote: agents are pretty prone to write markdown files but that doesn't really scale

takeaways.technique: Remote sandbox tool parity and debug access
takeaways.what_they_do: They noted local workstation MCP tools and apps may not match remote sandboxes, and they added SSH into sandboxes so agents or developers can inspect what is going on.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the tools that you have in your local workstation, your MCP tools, your locally running applications might not match what you have in a remote sandbox
